scenario.name: Docker Official Security, CISA & MITRE — Exposed Docker Daemon TCP Port 2375 API & Host Bind-Mount Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand city courthouse hall with fluted marble columns, an elevated wooden judge bench, a witness stand, and a brass wax-seal notary stamping desk. Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the courtroom marble columns in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press. The court bailiff audits the official notary stamp registry and discovers stamped certificates that were never entered into the judge’s docket book. In this scenario (T1613, Docker Official Security, CISA & MITRE, Exposed Docker Daemon TCP Port 2375 API & Host Bind-Mount Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API, then pOST /containers/create, then host Root Filesystem chroot. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API, then POST /containers/create, then Host Root Filesystem chroot, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1613 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Never bind dockerd to unencrypted TCP port 2375 (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375); bind strictly to unix:///var/run/docker.sock or enforce mutual TLS (--tlsverify) on TCP port 2376 with host firewall restrictions.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API Discovery (GET /v1.43/version & /containers/json)
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1613 - Container and Resource Discovery)
stages.description: Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the courtroom marble columns in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the court notary clerk go about their routine. When dockerd is started with -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375 without TLS (--tlsverify), any network client can reach the REST API over cleartext HTTP. The client queries GET /version and GET /containers/json to fingerprint the host kernel and running workloads (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with DaemonSocket=tcp://0.0.0.0:2375 , Unencrypted HTTP, RestEndpoint=GET /v1.43/version, RemoteClient=198.51.100.55:49210 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.title: Stage 2: POST /containers/create with HostConfig.Binds ["/:/hostfs"] & Privileged=true
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1610 - Deploy Container)
stages.description: Taking advantage of an unguarded moment at the notary desk, the forger lifts the impression of the courthouse wax seal and stamps a stack of unauthorized passes offline. Here in Step 2 inside the courthouse, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press without disturbing the sealed judicial record vault. Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -k docker_daemon_api -i runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -k docker_daemon_api -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1610 during "POST /containers/create with HostConfig.Binds ["/:/hostfs"] & Privileged=true" , The remote client sends POST /v1.43/containers/create specifying an Alpine image, HostConfig.Privileged=true, and HostConfig.Binds=["/:/hostfs:rw"], followed by POST /containers/<id>/start while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /v1.43/containers/create (Privileged=true, Binds=["/:/hostfs:rw"]) / ⇠#2 ACK 201) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 dockerd Daemon (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Linux Host Root Filesystem (/)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Host Root Filesystem chroot (/hostfs) & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Every forged document now bears the court’s own authentic wax emblem, letting the holder command authority in any neighboring municipal hall. In this final step inside the courthouse, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press until the court bailiff stamp registry catches the mismatch. Inside the started container, the entrypoint executes chroot /hostfs /bin/sh to operate directly inside the host root filesystem as UID 0, modifying /etc/crontab or /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, which Linux auditd and Falco eBPF sensors capture (logged in Linux Audit Event 161 with Syscall=sys_chroot , 161, TargetRootPath=/hostfs , Host Root /, FalcoAlert=Launch Privileged Container & Host Root Mount so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -f /etc/crontab -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -f /etc/crontab -i via crontab, passing the exact arguments, target paths, and prot so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Host Root Filesystem chroot , /hostfs & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit" , Inside the started container, the entrypoint executes chroot /hostfs /bin/sh to operate directly inside the host root filesystem as UID 0, modifying /etc/crontab or /root/ while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact docker ps --no-trunc --filter "status=running" runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , docker ps --no-trunc --filter "status=running" configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1611 during "Host Root Filesystem chroot , /hostfs & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ chroot /hostfs /bin/sh -c "cat /etc/shadow" / ⇠#3 ACK 161) from Node ③ (#3 dockerd Daemon (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375)) to Node ④ (#4 Privileged Container (/:/hostfs)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Linux Host Root Filesystem (/)).

keySpecs.value: Enable user namespaces (--userns-remap=default in /etc/docker/daemon.json) so container UID 0 maps to an unprivileged high UID on the host, and monitor chroot syscalls inside container cgroups.
